prior_report:
The exact corrected BaeSR record passes independent scientific review with explicit limits. Target SHA2561cf9262a0df376a19517b3f55ccaac67dacc8af8ce58bd8a1b2046e93a951824 covers13 paragraphs,15 edges,8 endpoint qualifiers,12 named identities,18 references and4 mappings. All six source-native reaction sides and the two separately identified donor-state interpretations remain intact. No blocking scientific finding remains.

Root personally read the complete1993 article text and its material figure pages; the complete2002 and2011 article material sequences and bibliographies; and all ten associated figure/table image bodies. Whole official HTML parsing proved the read material sequences complete. Every narrative paragraph and edge received an individual appraisal. The independent source reviewer separately checked all57 BioPAX objects, complete selected PWML frames,31locators,18 reference body/receipt bindings,12 issuer identities and4 mappings against actual originals. That review also read material current UniProt/sequence/chemical/GO/taxon frames; root does not relabel those as a second complete personal reading. Source scope and all exact pins are retained.

The review preserves source-state flattening, nil component coefficients, the phosphate acid/trianion conflict and the wrong native GO assertion without converting them into biochemical claims. ATP/ADP exact stereo mappings do not specify assay protonation. Historical BaeS differs from current P30847 by a length-changing sequence interval; historical BaeR reference equality does not resequence an assay plasmid. H250/D61 predictions remain distinct from demonstrated phosphorylation. Enriched1993 membrane/cytosolic fractions are not a purified pair, and inferred donor bookkeeping is not a measured balanced equation. The2002 expression/promoter results and2011 induction/phenotype results retain their construct, host and condition limits; they do not create direct ligand-binding or obligatory phosphorylation edges. The unavailable2005 full article remains reviewed-annotation-attributed.

Root and the independent source reviewer requested removal of one internal workflow sentence and two missing spaces. The original author implemented those exact three editorial substitutions. Root freshly verified complete115+2 author and16+2 successor closures and exact raw-text equivalence except those changes. All scientific statements, references, native IDs and evidence are unchanged. Original paragraph/edge appraisals and both author versions remain available; successor appraisals bind the corrected content.

The exact corrected draft has an external native preview. Its complete28+2 packet was freshly closed here. Root personally viewed the complete static light raster: both events and states are visible, with phosphate correctly disconnected. Long return paths, overlapping convergence labels, truncated qualifier descriptions and tall blank canvas are visual limits. The preview reviewer checked all13 paragraphs,15 arrows,8 qualifiers,18 references and anchors against complete DOM payloads. No interactive, responsive, dark, keyboard or print validation is claimed.

Two root review-helper failures are preserved: the author manifest uses relative paths rather than absolute paths, and the actual record field is source_mappings rather than mappings. The corrected check passed with complete original closure/equivalence coverage; neither error changed a product or scientific source. Earlier author/source-review acquisition and harness failures remain in their original packets.

This is a pre-integration scientific disposition, independent of scientific draft authorship. It is suitable for bounded source-authority design. It does not assert a completed authority import, maintained page, native saved review, full repository gates, publication, licensing clearance or source exhaustion.
source_report:
Independent bounded review of BaeSR author packet 243 — 2026-10-12

No blocking source, identity, locator, or native-state finding in the sealed author draft. Two small editorial corrections are appropriate in a successor: remove the final workflow sentence from the biological description, and change “the414–421” to “the 414–421” in the e09/e10 construct descriptions. The sealed author packet was not edited. This is a bounded source/identity review for the parent's scientific assessment, not authority integration, native adoption, or release acceptance.

Reviewed target: `/private/tmp/pathwaymech-next-243-author-20261012/draft/baesr-two-component-signal-transduction.yaml`, SHA256 `a90ea99b998fd229ce4a2b623e87235e5d22c4e351c8fefc005e8e18f4578236`. Handoff SHA256 `449a1a95b83d41dde2c7042899cbbae156e4595bc2aab6a42ff6fc9435b08a09`; manifest SHA256 `702a5f7c26b33442bb710eaacc92be476136ffdfa2e4407f83c00bcd82a98aad`.

The independent `check.py` completed successfully in `run-6.json` (exit 0). The exact command is recorded there: `/private/tmp/pathwaymech-next-195-20261011/.venv/bin/python /private/tmp/pathwaymech-next-243-source-identity-independent-review-20261012/check.py`. Its source hash and every original reference pin are in `checks.json`. The walk uses `os.walk(..., followlinks=False)` plus `lstat`, includes hidden and gitignored entries, compares the complete file and directory sets, and checks every manifest size/hash. Author closure is 115 artifacts plus two seals in 11 descendant directories; preflight closure is 256 plus two seals in nine directories. Neither packet contains symlinks or repeated file inodes. All 18 draft references equal their bound ledger references and whole original bodies; all 18 acquisition receipts bind the same body/hash and requested URL with HTTP 200. This does not turn unrelated failed/metadata-only acquisitions into primary evidence.

All 31 evidence locators were enumerated from the actual draft and freshly resolved against the appropriate original or reversible PWML reading derivative. Each XML locator selects exactly one element; JSON locators select actual current UniProt comment objects. For the PDF locators, an independent PDFKit extraction reads physical page 7 of the complete original PMID8282725 PDF. The original raw PWML fails strict XML parsing because of the unbound drawing `option` prefix. Exactly one 63-byte namespace insertion reconstructs the retained reading derivative, and reversing it reproduces every original byte. The derivative is not an issuing original. All 12 named draft ID/label pairs were independently matched to actual issuing subject frames, and all four mappings match the native source reference elements and current issuer identities.

The complete current and archived BioPAX trees were compared, including all 57 top-level objects, nested attributes and text. The current whole-object ledger and every whole object in all eight selected PWML kinds match the actual originals (outer serialization whitespace excluded). The only archive/current text changes are phosphate structure `[O-]P([O-])([O-])=O` to `OP(O)(O)=O`, formula `O4P` to `H3O4P`, and molecular weight `94.95342` to `97.9769`. Both complete PWML reactions independently yield six formal sides, all coefficient 1: 6144 consumes state4106 and ATP414, produces state4107 and ADP1034; 179009 consumes state12056 and produces state12057. The two BaeS donor sides e07/e08 are explicitly interpreted additions. They are not native equation members. BaeR states12056/12057 collapse to the same BioPAX protein on both sides; PWML distinguishes them and leaves BaeR component/cofactor coefficients nil. BaeS state4107 contains a protein modification linked to compound1104. BioPAX uses a complex and reciprocal intramolecular BindingFeatures, also attaching the same feature to the base protein: those represent an export state-encoding problem, not evidence of a physiological noncovalent complex or a prephosphorylated left reactant. No native Catalysis/Control/nextStep elements were found in either whole export. The draft appropriately grounds catalytic and ordering interpretations in biological evidence instead of array order.

The actual current UniProt scientific frames were read (description, genes, organism, comments and features), and complete material frames, references, sequences and cross-references were compared against both author's protein ledgers. The complete historical BAA03140.1 and D14054.1 records confirm 466-residue BaeS versus current P30847's 467 residues. Historical positions414–420 `VPATVPA` replace current414–421 `GSRNRASG`; all flanks match. Historical BaeR equals current P69228 over its complete 240 residues. D14054 includes three CDS entries, including an upstream partial CDS; its BaeS/BaeR coding intervals include stop codons. These reference comparisons do not resequence the historical assay plasmids. H250 and D61 exist at the stated current coordinates, but the residue modifications are ECO:0000255 PROSITE-ProRule annotations (PRU00107/PRU00169), not sites directly established in the 1993 assay. The draft preserves that distinction.

Bounded primary reading used actual page 7 of Nagasawa et al., rather than only an author assertion. It specifies pUC19/lac constructs in DZ225 ΔenvZ, urea-washed membrane and enriched cytosolic fractions, 0.05 mM gamma-labelled ATP, 50 mM KCl and 5 mM CaCl2. BaeS labelling and a BaeR-mobility band in the mixed-fraction assay support the stated interpretation, with the authors' own presumptive cognate-kinase language. They do not directly show donor dephosphorylation, a purified BaeS/BaeR pair, or residue-resolved phosphorylation. The draft's two interpreted donor sides, assay construct qualifications and separation from reference sequences are consistent with this evidence. I did not duplicate the parent's complete three-paper/ten-figure reading; that coverage remains in the parent's `read-coverage.json`. Other database-cited papers remain annotation-attributed, including the unavailable 2005 primary full text.

ATP and ADP match the complete ChEBI InChI, stereochemical InChIKey and formula of their neutral source-drawn species. These two exact chemical mappings do not assert the protonation state of the assay substrate. Native compound1104's current acid structure matches CHEBI:26078, while its retained CHEBI:18367/PubChem1061 references identify phosphate(3−); the whole PubChem body confirms charge −3 and the anionic InChI. The draft keeps this marker isolated from all 15 mechanistic edges, has no phosphate exact mapping, and does not equate free acid or phosphate(3−) with a protein-bound phosphoryl moiety. Native GO:0070258 identifies an active apicomplexan inner membrane pellicle complex; GO:0005886 is the appropriate curated plasma-membrane term and has bacterial inner membrane as a narrow synonym. GO:0005737 is cytoplasm. Actual direct NCBI taxonomy subjects distinguish E. coli562 and K-1283333; current UniProt chains and the four PWML state objects are K-12, while native BaeS protein and BioPAX pathway are species-scoped. No MG1655-only or pan-E. coli experimental claim follows.

All failed attempts remain visible in `preserved-failures.json` and numbered logs/source snapshots: missing lxml in bare Python, a list/dict inspection assumption, XML outer-tail comparison, unavailable pdftotext, Swift's default cache outside writable roots, and an initial wrong PubChem response-shape assumption. They were review environment/harness failures, not suppressed product failures. Run5 first passed; run6 added direct issuing-label equality for every named node and passed. No broad suite, full native builder, source refetch, SQL build/hash, maintained edit, Git mutation, or public action was performed. Writes are confined to this external review directory and a temporary Swift module cache.

prior_read_coverage.read_recovery: The initial combined bibliography output truncated 2011 references4–7; all1–8 reread in3b195d. Initial chemical-ledger combined read also truncated; it is not claimed complete here.

primary_judgments.judgment: Full-length pSU11S/pSU11R expressed in DZ225; BaeS in4Murea-washed membrane fraction and BaeR in45percent-saturation ammonium-sulfate cytosol. Fig8A/C supports ATP-dependent labeling and authors presumed cognate transfer, with vector control; not a purified pair, exact donor-loss assay, site-specific proof or physiological ligand experiment. H250/D61 conserved candidate sites inFig6. pSN25 truncated BasS is separate; OmpR cross-phosphorylation is separate.

Constructs distinct: altered pTrcBaeR last8residues replaced by17vectorresidues; intact pBADBaeR; separate CterminalValAspHis6 protein. Wholecell resistance/accumulation is contextual (notably deltaacrAB), promoter reporter and purified-tagged-protein EMSA support mdtA regulation. BaeS deletion does not abolish overexpression phenotype and binding preparation probably unphosphorylated. No obligatoryphosphorylation claim; no MdtD requirement or measured native oligomer stoichiometry.

Read all79articleblocks, all44bibliography entries, four figures and imageTable2. WT/mutant reporters support condition-specific flavonoid,tungstate,zinc/highindole induction; not direct BaeS ligand binding. MdtA complementation supports efflux-related interpretation, not purified substrate transport. Biofilm tests use2K1056/500uMindole and do not justify universal lack of BaeSR effect. Introductory dimer/activation assertions are not directly measured here.
